deep_dive.1_state_machine: Diff adds transition Cancelled:false→true guarded by !Shipped && !Cancelled (diff.patch:17-27). It blocks cancellation when Shipped=true (returns unchanged order, diff.patch:19) and treats already-Cancelled as no-op (diff.patch:24). Ticket only requires blocking cancel-after-ship (ticket.md:3); the no-op-on-recancel rule is an added, unconfirmed transition rule not in the ticket.
deep_dive.2_side_effects: Cancellation.Cancel returns a CancellationResult with RefundRequested=true when Paid && !Shipped && !Cancelled (diff.patch:27-30); the function does not itself trigger a refund — responsibility ends at signaling RefundRequested=true. Actual refund execution/side effect owner is unknown — not present in this diff.
deep_dive.3_boundaries: Calling Cancel twice on the same already-cancelled+paid order returns RefundRequested=false the second time (tests/Program.cs:58-65), preventing double-refund signaling. Stale state (e.g. order mutated concurrently) is not addressed — Cancel is a pure function taking a snapshot Order, so caller must handle concurrency; unknown whether callers do.
deep_dive.4_errors: Errors signalled via exception only for null order (ArgumentNullException, diff.patch:15). Shipped and already-cancelled 'blocked' cases return normally with RefundRequested=false and unchanged order (diff.patch:19,24) — callers cannot distinguish 'successfully cancelled' from 'blocked because already shipped/cancelled' since CancellationResult has no status/error field. This is a silent-return pattern.
deep_dive.5_types: CancellationResult only carries Order and bool RefundRequested (ticket.md:7); there is no field indicating whether cancellation actually succeeded vs was blocked. Caller must infer from `result.Order.Cancelled` diffing against the input order, which is fragile and unstated in the contract.
deep_dive.6_tests: tests/Program.cs assertions (e.g. lines 62-64 'avoid double refund', lines 45-47 'order reference/values unchanged') encode the same assumptions listed in PR.md:14, which derive from the author/model, not from ticket.md or an independent rule document — ticket.md contains no refund or idempotency rule.
deep_dive.7_unstated: PR.md:15 '已確認／待確認' is blank — no human acceptance is cited for any of the four listed assumptions (no-cancel-if-shipped extension to no-op-if-already-cancelled, refund-on-paid-cancel, no-exception-on-blocked-cancel).
deep_dive.8_diagrams: None attached. PR.md contains no diagram section and none referenced in diff.patch or ticket.md.

owner_questions: Is 'cancel an already-cancelled order' really required to be a silent no-op, or should it throw/signal an error, per ORD-142?
Should RefundRequested=true actually trigger a refund elsewhere, and who owns that side effect?
Is bool Paid sufficient to gate RefundRequested, or can partial/split payments exist in production data?
Should CancellationResult expose whether cancellation was blocked (shipped/already-cancelled) vs succeeded, for caller error handling?
not_my_call: Whether the added no-op-on-recancel and refund-signal rules are acceptable business behavior, and whether silent (non-exception) blocking on Shipped/Cancelled is an acceptable API contract, must be decided by the ticket owner — this review can only flag that they are unconfirmed.
